query: Microsoft fiscal year 2026 Q2 capital expenditure AI data center spending
normalized: 2026 ai capital center data expenditure fiscal microsoft q2 spending year

output.content:
Microsoft reported **$37.5 billion of capital expenditures in FY2026 Q2** (the quarter ended December 31, 2025), encompassing AI and broader cloud infrastructure investment. [[1]] 

About **two-thirds** of Q2 capex—approximately **$25 billion**—went to short-lived assets, principally GPUs and CPUs; the remaining roughly **$12.5 billion** funded long-lived infrastructure expected to support monetization for 15 years or more. [[1]] 

The data-center component also included **$6.7 billion of finance leases**, primarily for large data-center sites, while actual cash paid for PP&E was **$29.9 billion**. [[1]] 

Management said demand continued to exceed available supply, with investment directed at expanding Azure capacity, supporting first-party AI workloads such as Microsoft 365 Copilot and GitHub Copilot, increasing R&D compute allocations, and replacing end-of-life server and networking gear. [[1]] 

For FY2026 Q3, Microsoft initially guided capex to decline sequentially because of normal cloud-buildout variability and finance-lease delivery timing, while keeping the short-lived-asset mix similar to Q2. [[1]]

sources.title: Microsoft Fiscal Year 2026 Second Quarter Earnings Conference Call
